stem: Two lighting schedules produce the same calculated DLI, but one uses a higher PPFD for fewer hours. Which statement is most scientifically cautious?
choices: Matching DLI indicates a similar daily photon dose, but differences in instantaneous intensity and photoperiod can still influence plant response
Matching DLI makes the schedules biologically interchangeable if fixture spectrum and canopy temperature are also similar
The higher-PPFD schedule should produce the stronger response because a larger fraction of the daily photons arrive at greater instantaneous intensity
The longer-photoperiod schedule should produce the stronger response because spreading the same photon dose across more hours improves light-use efficiency
rationale: DLI summarizes daily photon dose, but plants can respond to instantaneous intensity and photoperiod as well. Equivalent DLI should not be assumed to guarantee identical biological outcomes.
